title: Recent-Purchase Cap on Total Loss Vehicle Value
content:
**Rule.** Under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), a recent-purchase cap limits the vehicle value paid to a loss payee. The starting value from which that vehicle value is figured is never more than the cap.

**Acquisition date.** The cap turns on the vehicle's original acquisition date. That date is recorded on the vehicle-added change for the coverage's VIN on any of the named insured's Owner Auto Policy terms.
- A renewal carries the vehicle over without a new change, so the change that first scheduled the vehicle is read.
- Of several such changes, the one with the latest change effective date is read.

**Days held.** These are counted in calendar days from that acquisition date to the date of loss. The date of loss is counted and the acquisition date is not.

**The cap.**
- **Held fewer than 180 days.** The cap is the coverage's value at binding.
- **Held at least 180 days but fewer than 365 days.** The cap is the value at binding multiplied by 1.10.
- **Held longer, or no acquisition date recorded.** There is no cap.

### Both sides of each boundary (hypothetical, value at binding 10,000.00 USD)

| Days held at the date of loss | Cap |
|---|---|
| 179 | 10,000.00 USD |
| 180 | 11,000.00 USD |
| 364 | 11,000.00 USD |
| 365 | No cap |
| No vehicle-added change with an acquisition date for the VIN | No cap |

A starting value of 11,800.00 USD is limited to 11,000.00 USD when the vehicle was held 200 days. It stays 11,800.00 USD when the vehicle was held 400 days.
